title: English Vocabulary in Use — Pre-intermediate and Intermediate · Units 75–76

units.title: Unit 75 — Fixed phrases
units.source: English Vocabulary in Use — Pre-intermediate and Intermediate (4th Edition); printed pages 156–157 (PDF pages 157–158).
units.bookTitle: English Vocabulary in Use — Pre-intermediate and Intermediate (4th Edition)
units.category: Idioms, fixed expressions and discourse markers
learningObjectives: Understand frequent idioms and fixed expressions as whole units rather than translating individual words.
Use time expressions to discuss future intervals, immediate action, repetition and progress up to now.
Use paired fixed phrases with and or or accurately and naturally.
Introduce advice, examples, opinions and topic changes with appropriate conversational phrases.
Understand the additional idioms and usage distinctions tested in exercises 75.1–75.4.

items.pt: expressão fixa; locução de uso consagrado
items.example: A fixed phrase often has a meaning that is not obvious from its parts.
items.note: A set group of words that is usually learned and used together.

items.example: The teacher explained an idiom that I had never heard before.
items.note: An expression whose meaning is not always predictable from the individual words.

items.example: My cousin called me out of the blue after ten years.
items.note: Unexpectedly, without warning; commonly follows a verb describing an event.

items.example: Her surname rings a bell, but I cannot remember where we met.
items.note: If a name or idea rings a bell, it sounds familiar; often used in questions.

items.example: You need to make up your mind before Friday.
items.note: Decide between alternatives; change the possessive for the person involved: make up my mind.

items.pt: livrar-se de algo; desfazer-se de algo
items.example: We should get rid of the broken chairs in the garage.
items.note: Remove, throw away, sell or otherwise dispose of something; of is required.

items.example: I was about to leave when the phone rang.
items.note: Be about to + infinitive means an action will happen very soon; use am, is, are, was or were.

items.pt: cair no choro; começar a chorar de repente
items.example: She burst into tears when she heard the news.
items.note: Suddenly start crying; burst has the same form in the past tense.

items.pt: exceto; com exceção de; além de
items.example: Everyone joined the walk apart from Nina.
items.note: Here means except for; in other contexts it may mean in addition to.

items.example: All the windows were clean except for the kitchen window.
items.note: Introduces an exception; close in meaning to apart from in this unit.

items.example: The results will be ready in four days' time.
items.note: The apostrophe follows the plural days; means four days from now, not a four-day duration.

items.example: We'll meet again in two weeks' time.
items.note: A useful replacement for in four days’ time; in + interval + time points to the future.

items.example: We visited the museum the week before last.
items.note: The week that came before last week, not simply last week.

items.example: The new timetable has worked well so far.
items.note: Up to the present point; often used with the present perfect.

items.example: Please call me at once if anything changes.
items.note: Immediately; in this use, equivalent to right away and straight away.

items.example: I replied to the invitation right away.
items.note: An immediate response or action; synonymous with at once.

items.example: We need to deal with that problem straight away.
items.note: Especially common in British English; means immediately.

items.pt: noite após noite; todas as noites seguidas
items.example: The neighbours played loud music night after night.
items.note: Repeated every night, usually over a period of time.

items.pt: dia após dia; dia depois de dia
items.example: Day after day, she practised until she felt confident.
items.note: The same situation continues or happens repeatedly over many days.

items.example: We still meet for coffee now and again.
items.note: Occasionally; close in meaning to now and then.

items.example: I listen to old songs now and then.
items.note: Another fixed phrase meaning occasionally.

items.example: I have one or two ideas for the presentation.
items.note: A small, not necessarily exact, number.

items.pt: paz e sossego; tranquilidade e silêncio
items.example: After work, I need a little peace and quiet.
items.note: A calm environment free from noise or interruption.

items.pt: para cima e para baixo; de um lado para o outro
items.example: We walked up and down the road looking for the address.
items.note: Back and forth along a place; this is the directional sense taught here.

items.pt: uma ou duas vezes; algumas vezes
items.example: I have tried that restaurant once or twice.
items.note: A few times; often an approximate rather than exact count.

items.example: Sooner or later, we will need to replace this computer.
items.note: Something will happen eventually, although the time is unknown.

items.pt: de tempos em tempos; de modo intermitente
items.example: They have been learning Spanish on and off for several years.
items.note: Intermittently, with breaks; introduced in exercise 75.1.

items.example: If I were you, I would check the address first.
items.note: A hypothetical way of giving advice; traditionally were even with I.

items.example: In general, buses are cheaper than taxis.
items.note: Broadly speaking; introduces what is usually true.

items.example: On the whole, the course was very useful.
items.note: Looking at a situation overall; a synonym of in general in many contexts.

items.example: Some cities, for instance Bristol, have excellent cycle routes.
items.note: Introduces a specific example; synonym of for example.

items.example: Try a lighter meal, for example a bowl of soup.
items.note: Introduces an illustration of a general point.

items.example: By the way, did you get my message yesterday?
items.note: Introduces a new or additional subject during a conversation.

items.example: To be honest, I found the film rather slow.
items.note: Signals that you are giving your real opinion, sometimes politely negative.

items.pt: sentir-se à vontade; sentir-se em casa
items.example: The team made me feel at home on my first day.
items.note: Feel comfortable, accepted and relaxed in a place or group; exercise 75.4.

items.pt: custar uma fortuna; custar muito caro
items.example: Our car repairs cost a fortune last month.
items.note: Be extremely expensive; an informal idiom tested in exercise 75.4.

items.pt: ficar de olho em algo; vigiar algo
items.example: Could you keep an eye on my suitcase for a minute?
items.note: Watch or look after something to keep it safe; the preposition on is essential.

items.word: on the tip of my tongue
items.example: Her name is on the tip of my tongue, but I cannot remember it.
items.note: You almost remember a word or name but cannot say it just yet; possessive changes.

items.pt: uma noite na rua se divertindo; uma noite de diversão pela cidade
items.example: We enjoyed a night on the town after the conference.
items.note: An evening out for entertainment, for example at restaurants or bars; informal.

items.pt: estar precisando de algo; algo cairia bem
items.example: I could do with a cup of tea after that long journey.
items.note: Informal phrase expressing that something would be useful or welcome.

sectionsChecked: A: Meaning of fixed phrases and idioms, including the illustrated emotional reaction
B: Time expressions and their synonymous variants
C: Fixed pairs joined by and/or
D: Fixed expressions introducing advice, opinions and examples

units.title: Unit 76 — Fixed phrases in conversation
units.source: English Vocabulary in Use — Pre-intermediate and Intermediate (4th Edition); printed pages 158–159 (PDF pages 159–160).
units.bookTitle: English Vocabulary in Use — Pre-intermediate and Intermediate (4th Edition)
units.category: Conversational responses and spoken discourse markers
learningObjectives: Recognise positive, negative and uncertain fixed responses, including their degree of certainty.
React naturally to surprising news, polite proposals, questions and requests.
Use conversational expressions such as have a word with, pay attention and in that case.
Understand informal fillers, approximation phrases and expressions for managing decisions.
Apply the conversational patterns reviewed in exercises 76.1–76.4.

items.example: I've no idea when the meeting finishes.
items.note: A natural spoken way to say I do not know. Also possible: I have no idea.

items.example: That depends on whether the weather improves.
items.note: A cautious answer when conditions determine the result; can be followed by on.

items.example: It depends on how much time we have.
items.note: A common alternative to that depends; not a definite yes or no.

items.pt: por que não?; claro, pode ser
items.example: We could meet after lunch. Why not?
items.note: Can indicate agreement to a suggestion, not just a literal question asking for reasons.

items.example: Did you enjoy the concert? Not really.
items.note: A soft or limited negative response; less direct than a firm no.

items.example: You want to speak to the manager? What for?
items.note: Informal question about the purpose or reason; not why for.

items.example: Could I take your car abroad? No way!
items.note: Strong, informal refusal or statement of impossibility; context matters.

items.example: Will he lend us his new bicycle? No chance.
items.note: Informal synonym of no way when denying a possibility or refusing.

items.pt: acho que sim; suponho que sim
items.example: Is the shop still open? I suppose so, but I am not certain.
items.note: A hesitant or not very strong yes; does not express complete certainty.

items.pt: não acreditei no que vi; fiquei de queixo caído
items.example: When I saw the mountain view, I couldn't believe my eyes.
items.note: Expresses great surprise at something seen; a past-tense idiom.

items.pt: você só pode estar brincando; não pode ser sério
items.example: You must be joking! The tickets cannot be that expensive.
items.note: Reaction to surprising news, whether unpleasant or pleasant.

items.example: You're joking! You really won the competition?
items.note: Common alternative to you must be joking; expresses disbelief or surprise.

items.pt: você está brincando; só pode ser brincadeira
items.example: You're kidding! They offered you the job already?
items.note: Informal synonym of you must be joking; often a positive surprised reaction.

items.example: I don't believe it! We won the final!
items.note: Exclamation of great surprise; not always a literal claim that someone is lying.

items.pt: conversar em particular com alguém; falar brevemente com alguém
items.example: I need to have a word with the supervisor after lunch.
items.note: Speak briefly with someone, often privately or about a particular issue.

items.example: It was, you know, a difficult decision for everyone.
items.note: A very common spoken filler; can also seek shared understanding.

items.example: Please pay attention to the safety instructions.
items.note: Listen or concentrate carefully; say pay attention, not give attention.

items.pt: esse tipo de coisa; coisas assim
items.example: They sell bread, cakes and that sort of thing.
items.note: Informal way to refer to other similar examples without listing them all.

items.pt: esse tipo de coisa; coisas desse tipo
items.example: She enjoys cycling, walking and that kind of thing.
items.note: Equivalent to that sort of thing; refers to similar activities or objects.

items.example: The bus has stopped running. In that case, we can take a taxi.
items.note: Introduces what should follow from the situation just described.

items.pt: sentir-se mal por algo; ficar chateado com algo
items.example: I feel bad about cancelling the appointment.
items.note: Feel sad, guilty or unhappy about an action or situation; follow with about.

items.pt: não conseguir evitar; não ter controle sobre isso
items.example: He laughs when he feels nervous, and he can't help it.
items.note: Be unable to stop or control a feeling or behaviour.

items.pt: esperar para ver; aguardar para saber o que acontece
items.example: We haven't received a reply, so let's wait and see.
items.note: Wait until events give more information instead of deciding immediately.

items.pt: e se...?; o que acontece se...?
items.example: What if the train is cancelled tomorrow?
items.note: Introduces a possible situation and asks what would happen; keep the question as a sentence in examples.

items.pt: mudar de ideia; mudar de opinião ou decisão
items.example: If you change your mind, we can book a different date.
items.note: Change a previous decision; use my, his, her, our or their as appropriate.

items.pt: meio que; mais ou menos; um tanto
items.example: The sky was sort of orange at sunset.
items.note: Informal approximation or softening expression; often pronounced sorta in rapid speech.

items.pt: meio que; mais ou menos; um tanto
items.example: I felt kind of tired after the trip.
items.note: Informal expression meaning rather, approximately or to some degree.

A: Language-help box on joking/kidding and surprise
B: Dialogue with private discussion, attention, possible actions, and decision-making
B: Language-help box on sort/kind of and that sort/kind of thing
